public_rationale: Only the firm part is scored: that generative AI costs would begin to eat into SaaS companies' margins or profits. The 'I imagine' follow-on about price rises or dropping tools is hedged and excluded. Figma, a public SaaS company, met the early-resolution rule. On its Q3 2025 earnings call, the CFO said the cost of serving Figma Make and other AI features to all customers 'impacted gross margin' (e1). Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 86% from 92% a year earlier (e2). Because he said only that this would 'begin', one clear, company-attributed case counts as support.
limitations: Rests on one company. Others may show no such erosion.
Figma's gross margin fell but it stayed profitable on a non-GAAP basis, so 'eat into' is met only in a modest sense.
Figma's profitability before this was not clearly 'tenuous'. That descriptive word in the claim is not tested.

criteria.contradiction_condition: No deadline, so it cannot be contradicted by the passage of time. It would be undercut only if SaaS companies broadly showed that AI features raised margins and none reported AI-driven margin erosion.
